text:
Nora P.: Doing a short link & SDK consistency sweep on the Dedicated Capacity docs. Goal: ensure terraform var names, SDK calls (py/go/ruby), and handbook anchors all line up before the next docs release. I'll open a single PR with small commits. Anyone object to that scope?
Ethan V.: +1. Can you also include a tiny Ruby example? We don't have one in the existing Quick Commands and infra folks sometimes ask.
Rina C.: Please standardize on `reserved_pool_replicas` in all terraform snippets. We've had several customers confused by `replicas` vs `reserved_pool_replicas`.
docs-bot: link-check: found broken anchor handbook/dedicated/operations.md#preemption-behaviour -> 404. Also detected redirect /handbook/dedicated/old-sla -> /handbook/dedicated/sla-and-slos (301). Files referencing broken anchor: handbook/dedicated/quickstart.md, handbook/dedicated/migration.md.
Nora P.: Thanks bot. I'll replace anchors to the new path /handbook/dedicated/behavior/preemption and add an internal note for the handbook team to create redirects for older anchors.
Ben S.: For SDK examples: Python should use `create_dedicated_capacity(..., scale_policy={'type':'autoscale','cooldown_seconds':300})`. Go should show a ScalePolicy struct. For Ruby let's mirror the Python payload shape so it's consistent.
Nora P.: Draft Ruby snippet I'm planning to add:
```ruby
require 'redwood'
client = Redwood::Client.new(ENV['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
client.create_dedicated_capacity(
  name: 'prod-reserved',
  gpu_type: 'a100',
  replicas: 3,
  scale_policy: { type: 'autoscale', cooldown_seconds: 300 },
  isolation: 'reserved-pool'
)
```
Maya L.: Add a one-line quota check comment above each snippet. "Always verify quota before provisioning" helps reduce onboarding noise.
Nora P.: Will do. Also adding a small appendix listing the canonical var names we want to keep across docs: terraform: `reserved_pool_replicas`, python/go/ruby SDK: `replicas` (SDK parameter), scale policy shape consistent across languages, and isolation values `tenant` | `reserved-pool`.
eng-runtime: FYI runtime default cooldown is 300s; we should show that number explicitly in the examples. Also please add a short "Runtime note" that preemption semantics are tracked in runtime ticket #451 and may change; docs should link to the ticket for now.
Rina C.: For migration docs, can we add a tiny checklist variant that emphasizes anchoring monitoring alerts for 24h and verifying canary routing? Keep it short and prescriptive.
Nora P.: Adding migration mini-checklist: (1) quota check, (2) provision in staging, (3) smoke test 50rps for 2m, (4) canary lift 10% increments, (5) monitor 24h. I'll include it in migration.md and reference it from Quickstart.
Ben S.: One more nit: ensure all examples use snake_case for terraform keys and consistent camel/snake for SDK payloads as per language style guides.
Nora P.: Good catch. I'll keep ruby/py using snake_case keys in hashes, go struct field names as exported CamelCase, and terraform snake_case.
docs-bot: PR created (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/10123 (Nora P.)
Ethan V.: I'll review the Ruby snippet and the anchor updates. Thanks for running the sweep.
Nora P.: Thanks everyone. I'll ping #docs-review and #eng-runtime once the PR is out of draft and mark follow-up TODOs for handbook redirects.
